title: bagOfWords

gpu_support.notes: `bagOfWords` builds host text-model metadata and currently stores dense host double counts.

description: `bagOfWords(documents)` creates a lightweight RunMat `bagOfWords` object from a `tokenizedDocument` compatibility object. `bagOfWords(uniqueWords, counts)` creates a model from an explicit vocabulary and count matrix.
behaviors: `bagOfWords` with no input creates an empty model.
`bagOfWords(words)` accepts a word vector as a single-document model.

`bagOfWords(uniqueWords, counts)` accepts a word vector and a nonnegative integer-valued count matrix whose columns match the vocabulary length. All eight integer classes are supported; values remain authoritative through exact validation and vocabulary-column filtering before one deliberate conversion into the double `Counts` property.
`uniqueWords` must not contain duplicate nonmissing words. Missing string entries are ignored along with their corresponding count columns.
The returned object stores `Vocabulary`, `Counts`, `NumWords`, and `NumDocuments` properties.

Counts are stored as a dense host double tensor with one row per document and one column per vocabulary word. Very large dense count matrices are rejected with a controlled error until native sparse bag storage is implemented.
GPU-resident inputs reject before provider access because `bagOfWords` exposes no interactive GPU-array input surface.
Native sparse bag storage and sparse-preserving GPU residency remain outside this slice.
Vocabulary order follows first token appearance for document input and the supplied order for explicit `uniqueWords` input.

examples.input:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["alpha beta"; "beta gamma"]);
bag = bagOfWords(documents)
examples.output: `bag.NumDocuments` is `2`, and `bag.Counts` has one column for each unique token.
`bag.Vocabulary` is `["alpha" "beta"]`, and `bag.Counts` is the supplied `2 x 2` count matrix.

faqs.question: Does `bagOfWords` use sparse matrices?
faqs.answer: Not in this slice. The compatibility object stores dense host counts and rejects very large dense count matrices. Sparse storage and provider-resident sparse paths remain broader runtime/model work.

faqs.question: Can `bagOfWords` consume raw document strings directly?
faqs.answer: No. Raw document arrays should first be converted with `tokenizedDocument`. A raw word vector is accepted as a single-document model.

faqs.question: Does `bagOfWords` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It builds a host text-model object and has no `runmat-accelerate` provider path. Resident inputs reject rather than gathering.

example.input:
bag = bagOfWords
bag = bagOfWords(documents)
bag = bagOfWords(words)
bag = bagOfWords(uniqueWords, counts)

points: `counts` must be a nonnegative integer-valued numeric matrix.
The number of columns in `counts` must match the number of vocabulary words.

gpu_residency: `bagOfWords` stores host text-model metadata and dense host double counts in this slice; resident inputs reject before provider access.
